q: After 5 heads in a row, tails is more likely next time.
why: Myth: the gambler's fallacy. The coin has no memory, so it's still 1/2.

q: Find P(at least one 6) in 2 rolls of a die.
why: Adding counts double six twice. Use the complement: 1 − (5/6)² = 11/36 ≈ 0.31.

q: A and B can't both happen, and both have P > 0. Are they independent?
o: No: if A happens, B can't, so A tells you about B
why: Independent means knowing A doesn't change the chance of B. Here knowing A makes P(B) drop to 0.

q: The probability of an event is greater than 1.
why: Probabilities go from 0 (impossible) to 1 (certain). A result above 1 means a mistake, often double counting.
